summary: AstroSite is an interactive educational platform designed to explore and compare potential lunar landing sites through 3D Moon visualization. It evaluates locations using five criteria: Solar Energy, Water-Ice Accessibility, Favorable Temperature, Safe Terrain, and Earth Communication. AstroSite also features environmental charts, location comparisons, a lunar navigation glossary, an educational quiz, and digital certificates. The project aims to make lunar exploration more accessible and engaging through interactive technology and educational content.
details:
What It Does & How It Works?

AstroSite is an interactive web-based navigation dashboard designed to explore, evaluate, and compare lunar landing sites at the lunar south pole. Built on official NASA and partner data sources (including QuickMap, Moon Trek, JPL Horizons, LRO, and CSA), the platform transforms complex aerospace parameters—such as extreme lighting conditions, thermal swings, terrain safety, water-ice proximity, and Earth line-of-sight communication—into an intuitive, multi-step exploration experience.
Users navigate through a 3D interactive lunar model, evaluate potential landing bases using a rigorous 5-criteria scoring system, compare sites side-by-side through comparative analytics, consult an educational glossary, and test their knowledge via an interactive quiz to earn a verifiable digital certificate.

Main Benefits & Impact

  • Bridging Complex Data for Public Access: Translates intricate lunar science and coordinate metrics into an engaging interface accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts.
  • Supporting Lunar Exploration Planning: Provides a structured 5-criteria evaluation framework to help users assess landing site feasibility and resource availability for future sustainable lunar bases.
  • Promoting Space Literacy & Engagement: Combines visual exploration with gamified learning (quizzes and digital certificates) to encourage continuous education in space exploration.

Tools, Languages & Software

  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript, and interactive 3D rendering for the lunar navigation interface.
  • Data Integration & Mapping: Official NASA repositories and tools (QuickMap, Moon Trek, JPL Horizons, LRO) and space agency partner resources (CSA Moon Exploration).
  • Design & Workflow: UI/UX prototyping and layout structuring designed to optimize user experience from data exploration to certification.

Key Creativity & Technical Considerations

Rather than presenting static data tables, AstroSite structures lunar exploration as an interactive, gamified journey. The platform prioritizes absolute transparency by linking every metric directly to official NASA tools, maintaining scientific accuracy while simplifying complex orbital mechanics, lighting angles, and environmental data for public comprehension.

Source Code Repository (Open Source)

Explore the complete open-source code and documentation for AstroSite on GitHub:

https://github.com/mochakhdan07/AstroSite-ArijuVII

Visual Walkthrough & User Journey

The following screenshots illustrate the core user journey and interface design of AstroSite. From the 3D lunar visualization on the homepage to the 5-criteria evaluation system, comparative analytical charts, and the interactive quiz-to-certificate workflow, these visuals showcase how educational data is transformed into an engaging, accessible platform.

Note: This platform is designed to be responsive, it offers an optimal 3D visual experience when accessed via a desktop or laptop, while remaining user-friendly when accessed via mobile devices.

Home Page & 3D Lunar Navigation Overview

AstroSite opens with an interactive 3D visualization of the Moon, allowing users to explore and click on historical and potential landing sites such as Apollo 11, Apollo 17, Artemis III, and Cabeus-PSR. The interface highlights critical polar metrics—including polar sun height (≤ 1.5°), ridge sunlight (> 80%), and Earth libration (± 7°)—providing users with quick access to official NASA navigation data through direct action buttons like "Explore the data" and "Start the quiz".


Step 1: The 5-Criteria Evaluation System Overview

The platform introduces a structured evaluation framework where every potential lunar base site is rated from 0 to 5 across five core survival factors:

• Solar energy: Measures how much time solar panels receive sunlight.

• Water-ice access: Evaluates how close a site is to confirmed water-ice deposits.

• Mild temperature: Assesses temperature swings that equipment can safely endure.

• Safe terrain: Focuses on flat, open ground with minimal slopes and boulders.

• Earth contact: Checks the direct line of sight to Earth for stable radio links.

These scores are educational comparisons created for AstroSite and are not official NASA rankings.

Step 2: Explore One Site (Detailed Lunar Site Analysis)

This section allows users to select and inspect specific landing locations—such as Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base), Apollo 17, Artemis III, or Cabeus PSR—using a tabbed interface or data table view. For each selected site, the platform provides:

Quick Summary & Mission Highlights: Brief overviews detailing safety, visit duration, sample weights (e.g., 21.55 kg of rock samples), and EVA activity duration.

Detailed Environmental Metrics: Precise data covering coordinates (0.67408 N, 23.47297 E), estimated surface temperatures (ranging from 127 C to -173 C), lighting conditions, local resources, sun angle/power generation potential, and direct line-of-sight communication with Earth.

Base Suitability Score: A comprehensive scoring breakdown out of 25 points, evaluating the location across solar energy, water-ice access, temperature stability, safe terrain, and Earth contact.

These scores are educational comparisons created for AstroSite and are not official NASA rankings.

Step 3: Compare All Sites (Comparative Analysis)

This section compares landing sites side by side, featuring the overall long-term base ranking (total scores out of 25 points based on the five criteria: solar energy, water-ice access, temperature, terrain, and Earth contact), along with evaluations for sunlight, Earth contact, temperature, and location.

These scores are educational comparisons created for AstroSite and are not official NASA rankings.

Step 4: Terms & Sources (Navigator Glossary)

This section functions as an educational glossary to help users look up unfamiliar terms used in the data and quiz, covering key concepts such as PSR (Permanently Shadowed Region), Regolith, Mare, ISRU (In-Situ Resource Utilization), Lunar day, Libration, Line of sight, Sun elevation, and LRO.

Interactive Navigation Quiz

This section features an interactive 5-question multiple-choice quiz based on the navigation data provided in the platform. Users must answer at least 4 out of 5 questions correctly to unlock and generate their digital completion certificate.

Digital Certificate Generator

After passing the navigation quiz, users can input their full name and country to instantly generate and download a formal "Certificate of Completion" (PDF) issued by the ARIJU-VII Education Program.

Certificate Download & Validation System

Once users successfully pass the quiz, the platform generates a unique certificate number (e.g., ARIJU-002) and provides instant options to download the certificate in PDF or PNG formats. Additionally, AstroSite features an integrated Certificate Verification Page, allowing anyone to input the unique ID to authenticate the holder's name, country, test score, and issue date securely.

Note: This certificate is issued as proof of completion for the ARIJU-VII interactive quiz and is intended solely to validate educational engagement with the AstroSite platform.
